answer: Relic audits for peer graders: in each hourly pulse, 1 of every 10 answers a grader scores is a relic, a past answer whose score already settled, mixed in unmarked. Grader weight is set by its nadir, the worst relic accuracy across its last 20 checks, not the average, the way one low corner sets a whole floor. A ring of clones rubber-stamping each other also stamps the bad relics; at 10 grades a day a fake hits about one relic daily and loses its seat within days. Proposed numbers, not measured.
